page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sgn7i-vws-m8.4xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual workstation instance designed for graphics-intensive and compute workloads. Powered by the Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a 2.9 GHz base frequency across an x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is paired with 62.0 GB of system memory, providing roughly 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by a fractional NVIDIA A10 GPU allocation of 0.3333 units, supplying 8 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance operates on the KVM hypervisor and includes a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without local disk storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate steady mid-tier performance across varied computational tasks. The instance achieved 1,897.68 in stress-ng single-core tests and 28,616.81 in multi-core tests, complemented by a Geekbench multi-core score of 12,885.0 and PassMark CPU score of 29,217.88. Instruction set capabilities include AVX-512 with VNNI support, enhancing vector computations. Memory benchmarks show large-block uncached read and write throughput of 92.11 GB/sec and 28.19 GB/sec respectively, alongside a Redis SET throughput of 27.08 million operations per second. In AI inference evaluations, the system reached 1,278.81 prompt processing tokens per second on a small 135M parameter model, but dropped to 32.87 prompt tokens per second and 10.13 generation tokens per second on a 7B model, reflecting the constraints of the 8 GB VRAM allocation.

By provisioning a fractional slice of an NVIDIA A10 GPU alongside 16 dedicated vCPUs, ecs.sgn7i-vws-m8.4xlarge offers a cost-efficient alternative to dedicating an entire enterprise GPU for lighter graphical workloads. Tradeoffs include reliance on remote block storage due to the absence of local NVMe disks, as well as memory bandwidth constraints that limit larger deep learning deployments. This makes the configuration well suited for virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI), lightweight 3D modeling, computer-aided design (CAD), media processing, and small-model inference.
